steps.content:
Two weeks later
Somewhere on the outskirts of Eastside
The car leaves the city, winding through overgrown paths before finally coming to a stop in front of a dilapidated building.
You step out and open the door for her, but she remains seated. Despite her attempt to hide it, the surprise on her face as she takes in the view outside doesn't escape your notice.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Is this your idea of punishment?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Call it a surprise. Spoiling it ahead of time would ruin the fun, wouldn't it?

This is the site of the old Redwood Orphanage. The ruins sit in silence atop a low hill. The fire has left the building unrecognizable—bricks and stone are showing through crumbling walls, and the gaping hollow windows look like empty eye sockets, staring out into nothing.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The crimes of Carl's family are still being looked into. There might be new leads here that the search team overlooked.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I think you can help with this. Consider it a chance to make amends. Can you accept that?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The MBCC certainly has an unconventional approach to discipline. Haven't I already told you everything you needed to know?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It wouldn't hurt to go over it again, would it? Think of it as field research for your new book. I heard you've been gathering material lately.
Clementine steps out of the car. For a brief moment, nostalgia flickers in her eyes. Before long though, her composure returns, that practiced smile sliding back into place.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: My, keeping tabs on me, are you? Did that child called Wynn tell you that? Are you helping her press me for my manuscript?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: A seasoned author works at her own pace. You don't need to worry about my progress, Chief. Besides, aren't we here on business?
She won't speak unless asked, and when you probe, she acts surprised. Clementine keeps everything locked away inside, all while maintaining that unbothered facade.
Without another word, she turns away and walks toward the ravaged building alone.
You hurry after her, signaling the security detail behind you to spread out. If there are any traces of the Sillage Society, they'll alert you immediately.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Ever since the Banbury family fell, many have been eyeing this land. The redevelopment plan is being voted on right before the Eastside residents. There shouldn't be any issues this time.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: That means this place will be torn down, huh...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes. This is your last chance to go inside.
Clementine closes her eyes. Years of rain have carved streaks down the charred walls, like tears running down a face. She gently traces them with her fingers.
After a long moment, she looks up. Birds are flying peacefully above the trees overhead.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The smell of smoke... is gone. Aside from the fire, will anyone even remember what happened here?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you're willing to talk about it, I'll make sure to remember. Anything goes.
You seize the opportunity, but she merely gives you a quiet smile and a knowing glance, as if she'd casually cast a line and baited out your true intentions just like that.
You make a quick recovery, keeping your expression serious.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This is also for the investigation. You were there, so you'd know more about Redwood Orphanage than any of us.

You expect her to dodge the question again, or perhaps throw you another puzzle and watch you struggle for answers. However, all she does is pause for a moment before walking straight toward the desolate, debris-strewn foyer.
[Scene Change: Interior]
Clementine's steps are light as she spreads her arms wide, just like a gracious host would when welcoming a guest into a home she's lived in for years.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: This was the reading room. Annie would play with her teddy bear here. The shelves were filled with fairy tales donated by kind souls, and there was a bean bag chair in the corner.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The filling was buckwheat. On sunny days like this, we'd take it outside to air it out. It smelled wonderful—like a wheat field at harvest.
It is indeed sunny today. You can almost smell the scent she's describing.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Come, feel this.

Clementine takes your hand and guides it to a series of notches carved into the doorframe at varying heights. There are markings beside them, but they've long since faded. You glance at her questioningly.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: This is where we'd measure everyone's height. It was an annual tradition, and the children always looked forward to it.
You trace your fingers along the marks. The highest line on the doorframe barely reaches your chest.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The orphanage was always short-staffed back then. I was the oldest, so I helped look after the younger children too.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's hard to picture what you were like back then. Did you put on a stern face to keep everyone in line, or did you run around and play with them?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: A bit of both. Some thought I was too quiet and serious. Others said I was full of clever schemes and good at getting people to do what I wanted.
She leads you to a side room. This must have been the kitchen. The stove beneath the window is covered in a thick layer of ash, and a few small bowls sit stacked beside it.
Clementine crouches down, moves the bowls aside, and taps the floor. She quickly locates a hollow brick and lifts it onto the stove.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: With this brick, any of the older children could climb right through the window.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: There's a small grove just outside. On nights when the moon was bright, we'd sneak out. Since we're pretty much in the countryside, we could go fishing, catch rabbits, or head to the nearby campgrounds for bonfire nights.

You gaze at the small patch of blue sky visible through the window. For a moment, you can almost see young Clementine, bathed in moonlight, perched on the windowsill. There, a world of wonder and freedom lay just beyond her reach.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Now you know what kind of child I was.
She narrows her eyes with that signature half-smile of hers. You can't help but smile back.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The caretakers never caught you?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: A few times, they did. When too many of us tried to sneak out at once, the old Director would stand right here in her faded blue apron. She'd tell us to slow down, and not to kick up dust into the bowls.
Clementine stands behind the door, her toes lightly scuffing at the ashes on the floor.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But that one time... only that one time, she told us to run faster.
[Flashback Filter: Fire Background]
She turns around and takes a deep breath. You wait quietly, giving her space.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Well, I've told you enough about this place. Let's move on.
She beckons to you and starts moving forward once more. You pass through the ash-gray main building and reach the courtyard.
[Scene Change]
The sun is blinding. She suddenly stops in the shade. Before you lies a scene of vibrant life—a stark contrast to the desolation you've seen so far.

The old tree in the courtyard is split. One half is grotesquely charred and has withered, while the other is bursting with new life. Its branches sag heavily toward the ground, nearly concealing an old tire that once served as a swing.
Clementine leads you beneath the tree, pushing aside the thorny branches. The soil is soft, so she was able to dig up a metal box with ease.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: It's still here, just as I thought.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: A time capsule. We read about them in a book and decided to bury one. We promised to come back and open it together when we grew up.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You going to open it?
Clementine slowly opens the box that has been sealed away for years. Perhaps the soil provided good protection—the metal hasn't oxidized too badly, and the contents inside still retain their shape.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The dried flowers were made by Viola. She wanted to open a flower shop in town. She said she'd pick the prettiest ones from the backyard, and once she earned enough money, she'd plant even more beautiful flowers around the Redwood.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The old magnifying glass belonged to Mrs. Jones. It was so worn down it couldn't be used anymore, but Searle put it in anyway.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: That child wanted to be an accountant. He'd help the butcher shop with their books and was always quick and accurate. The owner would often send him home with spare ribs.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Why's there a tooth here?
Clementine laughs. For a brief moment, warmth returns to her pale face, and you can see color in her cheeks. She gently picks up the tiny tooth.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Nana. She'd become flushed whenever she got excited. Her wish was to grow up as fast as she could, so she put in her baby tooth. If she were still here... she'd be a young lady by now.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And you? What did you put in?
Clementine smiles. She pulls out a manuscript from the very bottom of the capsule. The pages have yellowed with age, and are covered in dense handwriting.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This is... you wrote this?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Surprised? My very first work was a fantasy story to keep the kids entertained. I wrote everyone from Redwood into it—each of them had their own unique role. They all went on their own unique adventures.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I was planning to write them all as grown-ups too one day... Too bad I'll never get the chance.
The yellow pages have grown brittle with time. If Clementine were even a little careless, they'd be torn apart. She places them back gently, her movements as light as her tone.
She recounts these memories quietly. You know those people and that time are lost forever. All you can offer is a little comfort.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: While we were apart, I read your stories.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Annie, Viola, Searle, Nana... All of their names appear in your books. You made them into detectives, officers of the law, and so on, turning them into everything good and bright.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: They live on through your stories, Clementine. They've grown up alongside you, seen the world through your eyes, expressed their joys and sorrows through your words...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What you've done means more than anything else ever could.
Your gaze is calm and unwavering. Clementine stares at you for a bit, stunned, before quickly looking away.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Haha... I've never heard a review quite like that before.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Readers only care about whether the crime is thrilling enough, and whether the twists are shocking enough. Meanwhile, the media only cares about what angle I'll take for my next book, and whether it'll break sales records.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You're the only one who seems to pay attention to me as a person.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But at the MBCC, everyone's like that. They care about you as a person—not as some bestselling author, but as <color=#fb9259>Sinner Clementine</color>.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Raven wants to invite you to teach at the school. She's already on the third draft of the invitation, which is completely unlike her. She's usually the type to just get things done.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yugu wants to talk with you about writing. She knows you like to drink, so she had a field agent bring back some Eastian liquor. Then there's Wynn, who basically sees you as the center of her universe. She's constantly talking about your new book.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...When did all this happen?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You simply didn't notice since you've been so distracted lately. Everyone cares a lot about you, you know.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Look up, Clementine. Your revenge is over. You're not alone anymore.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Step into the light and keep writing. Trust me, more people will find their way into your stories. The children will meet new companions, and readers will draw courage and comfort from your words, just like they did back at Redwood.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So...
Please don't disappear on your own again. Don't give up, and don't walk into the darkness so readily.
You don't finish. Clementine lifts her head, wearing a vague smile. What she says next catches you off guard.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I see... I've been wondering why you decided to bring me here for a while now. What evidence could possibly be here that you and your colleagues haven't found after all this time?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: And then... it came to me.
She raises her hand, her fingertips trailing across your cheek.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You've been monitoring that safe house the whole time, haven't you? You knew all along that the Sillage Society sent me an invitation.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: When did you figure it out? Wait, if you already knew all this, why didn't you say anything—
Her hands lift your face, tilting your head up until your eyes meet Clementine's.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: She wanders far and wide, drifting ceaselessly, all because fate has denied her the chance to remain by your side.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: She becomes lost in reverie from the mere thought of you, just like when she gazes at the moon. And somehow, a miracle unfolds...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Shh, my dear detective. Who taught you those lines? It's certainly very... old-fashioned, but charming nonetheless. Are you trying to win me over with that?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No, that's not it...
You quietly ready your shackles. Unless absolutely necessary, you'd rather not force her compliance, since doing so would only defeat the purpose of coming here.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I just hope you'll think this through before you make your choice. Redwood's revenge is over. You can move forward now. There's no need to...
Before you can finish, a sickeningly sweet fragrance assaults your senses. Your scalp prickles in alarm, and you quickly tilt your head to the side.
Thunk! A bullet silently flies past your cheek and embeds itself in the tree trunk behind you.

The silence of the forest shatters. In the shadows of the ruins and crumbling walls, several dark figures have appeared, seemingly out of nowhere. They blend in almost seamlessly with the debris, their movements restrained, positions scattered. Yet, they've managed to perfectly encircle you.
At this distance, and from these angles... they couldn't have just arrived. Why didn't you receive any warning? Where are your lookouts?
You whip your head toward Clementine. Her expression is just as grim.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...Heh. Looks like my future colleagues have come to expedite my onboarding.
As she speaks, a second volley of gunfire erupts. This time, you both retreat in unison, taking cover behind an old tree.

options: You've already agreed to join them?

choices.text: You've already agreed to join them?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Not yet. But...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: What if I actually chose to join them?
You can't make out Clementine's face. Between ragged breaths, all you hear is her hushed voice.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Truth be told, my hands are hardly any cleaner than theirs. When I was at my lowest, it wasn't the law or justice that came to my aid—it was people like them.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You've said it yourself. What matters is who wields the blade. If I can use their dirty weapon to exterminate more vermin... perhaps that's not so bad either.
Clementine's voice drops lower and lower, nearly drowned out by the gunfire around you. Still, you hear every word.

options: Unfortunately, your resignation will not be approved.

choices.text: Unfortunately, your resignation will not be approved.

steps.content: Spending too much time with those Sinners must be rubbing off on you. You click your tongue and peek out from cover to return fire.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The path downward is always the easiest to take. But I've seen what happens when hatred consumes someone. It doesn't make things easier, it just turns you into the same bastards you despise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I won't let you go with them. Not before I fulfill our promise. And even if you leave, I won't give up. I'll find you again, no matter how many times.
You pivot to dodge an incoming attack. For the first time, you see unmistakable surprise written all over Clementine's face.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Heh... You always manage to catch me off guard.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Stay hidden. Don't come out.
Clementine pushes you back and positions herself on the outer edge of the cover.
The volley of bullets finally comes to a stop. Dark figures emerge from the forest, approaching slowly before halting at a safe distance. They're waiting for Clementine's answer.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I told you I'd reach out when I was ready. What's this? Do you perhaps regret giving me so much time? Or do you just not trust me?

steps.speaker: Assassin
steps.content: ...The deadline is approaching.

steps.speaker: Assassin
steps.content: All we need is your brilliant mind... to help us eliminate our enemies. Those wicked trash you've condemned so much yourself.
The assassin's gun shifts slightly, aiming straight at the tree trunk concealing you.

steps.speaker: Assassin
steps.content: Or... you can be buried here alongside the one who knows too much.
The sickeningly sweet scent stirs in the air once more, and you instinctively hold your breath.
Clementine takes another step forward. She raises her hand, seemingly to reach out and accept their offer.

But in the next instant, the air warps with Mania. The lead assassin's body goes rigid before collapsing silently to the ground. The second wasn't even able to turn before their breath falters and their gun drops.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I don't like being forced into anything.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: As a writer, I prefer to keep the pen in my own hand.
Clementine's answer is clear. Without another word, three assassins burst out from the shadows in unison, blades converging from three directions at once.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Watch out!
The situation is dire. You abandon cover and lunge forward, trying to intercept one of the daggers aimed at Clementine.
But Clementine is faster. She raises her gun.
Bang! The first shot deflects the dagger aimed at your face. And in the next instant, the second and third bullets knock away the remaining blades in quick succession.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Chief, I appreciate you trying to shield me. But in situations like these... the gun is quicker, don't you think?
Mania surges from Clementine. Corruption spreads out from the butterfly-shaped ornament she's wearing.

At the same time, crimson lines erupt from beneath her feet, expanding across the courtyard floor like blood vessels within moments. Wherever they reach, the assassins all collapse to their knees in agony.
The assassins had anticipated Clementine's refusal all along, and Clementine was waiting for precisely this moment. She needed them to draw closer, right into the range of her power.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: How unfortunate. You should have at least done your research on my ability.

Clementine touches the assassins, and her Mania immediately seizes control of their bodies, forcing them to turn their daggers toward their own throats. Their muscles tremble violently, the last shred of instinct fighting against the overwhelming compulsion.
The Mania surging from Clementine intensifies. The butterfly ornament at her neck seems to pulse with life, as though nourished by her power, wings poised to take flight at any moment.
You sense massive torrents of uncontrolled Mania pouring from Clementine's frail frame. The color drains rapidly from her face.
Her power comes at a cost. That is to say, her own life.

options: Clementine! Don't let it consume you!

choices.text: Clementine! Don't let it consume you!

steps.content: The woman at the eye of the Mania storm hears your voice and turns her face toward you. A faint smile plays on her lips as they move. It seems she's trying to tell you something.

What is she saying? You can't make out the words. You had intended to place the shackles on her according to Clementine's own wishes, but the situation has turned critical—if you don't act now, she'll either lose control or die. There's no time to hesitate!
You push through the torrents of Mania surging from Clementine, inching closer and closer until you finally grasp her hand.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Clementine! Wake up!
Pure Mania knows no allies or enemies. Now it turns on you.

Piercing crimson light floods your vision as the shackles bridge your consciousness with hers. Her mind feels like sand slipping through your fingers, plummeting toward darkness so rapidly you can barely hold on.
You feel her vital signs fading. You try to use the shackles to shoulder her burden, but instead, you're dragged alongside her into the endless void...
